winner.title: How to make Iraqi grilled fish | Dine & Discover

evidence.authenticity: Iraqi-linked author; explains the traditional carp, lemon and tamarind, open-fire Tigris method and that this version adds spices and uses bream for indoor grill/oven; pairs with amba, pickles, vermicelli rice. Still a home adaptation.
evidence.precision: Few weights (tsp/tbsp spices, '1 medium onion', '6 fresh tomatoes', '1 large sea bream'); no fish weight; sumac and salt unmeasured; only cue is marinade thickening and mango to pulp; no cue for fish doneness (10-12 min only); no pan size.
evidence.testing: No test-kitchen sign; brief context but little explanation of why.
evidence.photos: Three images (finished dish, amba, fish); no process stages.
evidence.efficiency: Prep stated as 2 hours and cook 45 min, which is loose; marinade and amba are made in parallel with no wasted steps.
evidence.access: Tamarind paste, dried lime powder, sumac are specialty but available at Middle Eastern grocers; no explicit substitutions.

winner.why: Most traditional framing and a full amba companion, ahead of the runner-up, but still under 60 because it has no fish doneness cue or weights.

runnerUp.title: sweet, sour, and spicy masgouf

evidence.authenticity: American blogger; uses fillets, curry powder, brown sugar and a tomato topping, a simplified adaptation of masgouf.
evidence.precision: US volumes and fish weight (10 to 12 oz); doneness cue 'until flaky' plus 6 minute minimum; no temperatures or pan size.
evidence.testing: Blog author, notes on fish and marinating times and broiler variation; no test kitchen.
evidence.photos: imagesOnPage 17 but none in schema steps; not confirmed as process shots.
evidence.efficiency: About 1 hour total; marinate and make topping in parallel.
evidence.access: All supermarket items; tamarind paste is footnoted.

runnerUp.why: Clearer cues but a further departure from traditional masgouf.

candidates.disqualified: Uses salmon, broiled with tomatoes; not recognizably masgouf
Herby branzino 'inspired by' masgouf, not the dish
No named author, aggregator/wiki copy, no photos
